objective: Deliver lightweight Android Wall video first-frame poster, same-URI player handoff into fullscreen, adaptive buffering and Connect initial-scroll stabilization; preserve native advertisements and signed media permissions.
productionBaselineEvidence: Inspected GitHub main source commit 0ee57887c991d23472cdf1f9b849bce945792910 (2026-11-17). Did not independently verify production OTA fingerprint, installed Android runtime, actual network rebuffer counts or RC device performance. DEV-only branch until full release QA.
chosenApproach: Use Expo SDK 57 onFirstFrameRender instead of playingChange to remove the poster, retain Android Expo player across a single committed inline-to-modal surface detach with a short bounded lease, adapt modest buffer thresholds using the existing network subscription; replace timed double scroll anchoring with a post-layout frame plus the content-size event as fallback.
alternativeApproaches: Download entire video before fullscreen (rejected: high data, memory, startup cost)
Render same Android player into two VideoViews simultaneously (rejected: Expo/Media3 limitation)
Replace native IMA ad player with generic ExpoVideo (rejected: breaks monetization)
Run repeated delayed scrollToEnd calls (rejected: causes Connect rebound)
selectionRationale: Native SDK-supported first-frame display signal and bounded player handoff reduce restart cost without background full-video fetches, extra retained decoders or broad infrastructure changes. Connected scroll and read receipt branches remain intact.
preserveBehaviors: Signed URL rotation never shares cached private media under a new URL
Google IMA in-stream ads and existing Wall companion/Reels placements remain live
Weak-network playback retry, zoom/Fill/Fit and same session audio controls remain available
Connect personal and scope messages, older paging, offline cache, read receipts and PTT/calls preserved
Screen navigation, Wall list, scoped feed and existing OTA identity unchanged
acceptanceChecks: Wall poster remains until onFirstFrameRender on native VideoView
Android fullscreen opens after inline VideoView detach; same URI reuses same player, avoiding second player allocation
Pausing, closing, fast swiping and signed URL renewal release players safely; cache stays 256 MB LRU
On limited network preserve user playback with a modest additional safety buffer; do not pre-download full videos
Connect opening stays at latest without two timer-driven scroll jumps; older and sender scrolling preserved
No unexpected IMA/ad interaction; run regression, TypeScript/build gates and native staging QA before RC/OTA
